BiblicalUsage: A horror, an object of trembling — the word is what God says His people will become to the nations when they turn away. Jeremiah repeats it through the judgment oracles: removed into all kingdoms, made a horror, a hissing, a reproach. It is not a feeling but a condition: a people held up as a warning to everyone who sees them.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the horror language is the hardest kind of mercy to hear. God does not hide what unfaithfulness costs — He names it plainly, so that the warning might turn a heart back before the sentence falls. My position is that a God who warns this plainly is a God who still wants His people to come home.
